e: Wilson disease is a treatable/reversible copper-storage disorder (chelation) — unlike the other progressive neurodegenerations listed.
Systemic sclerosis → patchy myocardial fibrosis from microvascular disease → dilated-cardiomyopathy-like picture, its most characteristic cardiac lesion.
Hearing impairment contributes least directly to falls compared to balance disturbance, muscle weakness or joint disease.
Frailty is driven mainly by sarcopenia — ↓es muscle mass & strength.
First step in malignancy-related hypercalcemia = aggressive isotonic saline volume expansion before bisphosphonates.
Refeeding syndrome: insulin surge drives phosphate intracellularly → hypophosphatemia is the key, most characteristic abnormality.
CD4 <40 c̅ ring-enhancing brain lesion → toxoplasma encephalitis is the most likely (usually multiple lesions, vs solitary in lymphoma).
ST elevation in II, III, aVF = inferior MI → right coronary artery occlusion (supplies inferior wall in most people).
Ann Arbor 'bulky' (X) modifier = mediastinal mass width >1/3 of the maximum intrathoracic diameter on CXR.

Boutonniere: PIP flexion c̅ DIP hyperextension (central slip rupture).
Swan neck: PIP hyperextension c̅ DIP flexion.
Horner + facial anhidrosis → lesion proximal to carotid bifurcation (sympathetic chain).
HOCM (asymmetric septal hypertrophy, AD) – commonest cause of sudden death in young athletes; screen relatives.
Variceal bleed c̅ hypotension: avoid β-blocker (used for prophylaxis); give octreotide, antibiotics, endoscopy.
GOLD: FEV₁ <30% predicted → chronic respiratory failure/resting hypoxemia.

Severe COPD exacerbation: bronchodilators + systemic steroids + antibiotics (↑ sputum).
Antivirals not indicated.
COPD: lung compliance ↑es (loss of elastic recoil in emphysema), not decreased.
Prolonged febrile neutropenia is the highest-risk setting for invasive aspergillosis.

Clonus/hyperreflexia (UMN signs) suggest compressive myelopathy.
Hypotonia/absent Babinski → LMN.
Dengue c̅ stable vitals & no bleeding: paracetamol alone; no antibiotics/steroids/platelets.
DCM predisposes to LV thrombus & AF → anticoagulation considered (esp. very low EF).
Huntington's: chorea + personality change/dementia; MRI shows caudate atrophy.

Tricuspid stenosis → RA enlargement → tall 'giant' P wave.
MS → broad notched P mitrale.
Anemia, fever, thyrotoxicosis → high-output failure; high salt → volume overload.
Serum ACTH & cortisol separate causes: low ACTH + low cortisol = exogenous (iatrogenic) steroid excess.
Conn's: Na⁺ normal/mildly ↑ (aldosterone escape); hypokalemia, HTN, alkalosis are typical.
Most berry aneurysms arise at the anterior communicating/ACA junction.

DVT risks: prolonged immobilisation, smoking, OCPs.
Hypothyroidism is not a recognised risk.

DKA & starvation ketosis → high anion gap (ketoanions).
Vomiting → metabolic alkalosis.
Sjögren (sicca + RTA c̅ hypokalemia): Schirmer's test + anti-Ro/La autoantibodies.
Cushingoid features in a child: most commonly exogenous (iatrogenic) steroids.
